title: Commitment brackets and gradated scope release plan
creator: Emily Chen
description:
Problem: Teams are overcommitting scope early in cycles because the current all-or-nothing commit model forces binary decisions that create frequent mid-cycle reheats. We need an explicit mechanism to commit in graduated bands ('brackets') so product leads can lock in critical outcomes while leaving quantified optional scope that can be deferred or reallocated without drama.

This ticket defines the policy, gating rules, staffing allocation heuristics, and communication templates for a 'commitment bracket' model and a complementary gradated scope release plan that operates at initiative and feature levels.
context:
Current practice: teams choose a single committed scope at the start of the cycle and manage exceptions via ad-hoc surge lanes and manual scope cuts. Outcomes: fragile schedules, reactive staffing moves, and unclear decision authority when tradeoffs are required.

Design principles: 1) make commitments explicit and tiered, 2) make staffing signals low-friction and time-boxed, 3) separate must-have outcomes from nice-to-have experiments, 4) keep rollback paths and measurable success criteria for every bracket.
goals: 1) Reduce mid-cycle scope panic by 50% for participating initiatives in two cycles. 2) Increase on-schedule delivery for P0 scope by 20% vs prior quarter. 3) Create a transparent escalation path so that >90% of scope cuts follow the bracket rules (not ad-hoc).
success_metrics:
- % of initiatives adopting commitment brackets within 2 cycles
- # of mid-cycle unplanned reassignments (target -50%)
- On-time delivery rate for bracket-1 outcomes (target +20%)
- Mean time to decision for scope cuts (target <48h where required)
proposed_workflow: 1) Planning phase (week -1 to 0): PMs define three brackets per initiative (Core, Stretch A, Stretch B) with explicit acceptance criteria and estimate points per bracket. 2) Staffing reservation: Core bracket gets firm staffing commit (FTE-days) reserved from the planning pool; Stretch brackets get soft reserves that can be reclaimed. 3) Gate days: Day 10 and Day 20 of the cycle are formal gate checkpoints to re-evaluate Stretch tiers. 4) Execution: If Core is blocked, automatic escalation to program lead with a 24h resolution SLA. 5) Release: publish bracket status to the console and announce via cycle status channel.
decision_matrix:
- If Core is green -> preserve staffing.
- If Core is behind >50% of acceptance criteria by gate -> trigger fast triage and possible borrow from Stretch A.
- If Core is blocked by external dependency -> escalate to PM director with proposed mitigation or scope swap.
- Stretch A and B are candidates for deferral; defer when cumulative risk-adjusted velocity drops below threshold defined in plan (default 0.75 of expected velocity).
staffing_rules:
- Core bracket: dedicated FTE allocation equals estimate. These seats are sacrosanct for the cycle unless mutually agreed in a documented swap.
- Stretch A: reserve up to 60% of required FTE as 'float' from the cycle buffer; float can be reassigned if Core needs additional capacity.
- Stretch B: optional, no reservation; filled opportunistically.
- Rotation: every 6 cycles rotate one engineer out of core allocations into a cross-initiative zone to reduce single-team burnout and preserve knowledge sharing.
- Hiring/temps: use contract buffer only for non-core stretch work unless approved by ENG leadership.
scope_cut_rules:
- Cuts must be expressed as removing a named bracket or defined feature slice; avoid ad-hoc item-level deletions without traceable rationale.
- Prioritization order for cuts: Stretch B -> Stretch A slice -> Re-scope non-critical acceptance criteria -> Avoid touching Core unless critical.
- Any cut that affects customer SLAs must be triaged with Customer Success and documented.
- Cuts greater than 20% of total initiative points require PM director sign-off and a public note in the cycle ledger.
communications:
- Template messages for gate outcomes to be published to #cycle-status and the initiative doc.
- Weekly one-slide update for exec sync showing bracket health (green/amber/red), staffing leaks, and recommended decisions.
- Post-mortem for any initiative where Core failed to deliver; include root cause and actions.
timeline: Week -2: PMs draft brackets and acceptance criteria; Week -1: Review with ENG leads and capacity owner; Week 0: Finalize brackets and reserve staffing; Week 1: Cycle starts; Day 10 & Day 20 gates; Week 5: soft freeze and final delivery; Week 6: ship and post-mortem if applicable.
stakeholders: PMs: define brackets and acceptance criteria; ENG leads: confirm staffing reserves; Capacity owner: maintain cycle buffer ledger; Design: align on acceptance criteria for UX. Exec sponsor: VP Product. Legal/Compliance: review if release touches regulated customers.
risks:
- Overly conservative brackets reduce throughput. Mitigation: monitor adoption and iterate brackets sizing.
- Teams may game stretch estimates to protect Core. Mitigation: random sample audit and compare historical velocity.
- Insufficient cycle buffer leads to frequent reclamation and morale issues. Mitigation: adjust buffer sizing after two cycles based on telemetry.
next_steps:
1) Pilot three initiatives this cycle (identify candidates by EOD Friday). 2) Create bracket template in Confluence and a lightweight form for PMs to submit reserves. 3) Capacity owner to model buffer sizes and publish recommended reserves by next week. 4) Schedule a 60-minute rollout training for PMs and ENG leads. 5) Collect feedback after first gate and iterate policy.

Owners: Emily Chen (PM process owner), Jordan Patel (capacity modeling).
acceptance_criteria:
- Confluence template exists and is linked from the initiative doc.
- At least 3 initiatives have brackets defined and staffing reserves recorded before cycle start.
- Gate checklist and messaging templates posted to the team repo.
- Capacity model shows buffer allocation and projected reclaim thresholds documented.
- Pilot retrospectives scheduled for the week after ship.
